agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# bat

bat is a human-friendly command-line HTTP client for testing, debugging, and interacting with HTTP servers.

Main features:

- Expressive and intuitive syntax for building HTTP requests
- Built-in JSON support
- Form and file upload support
- Support for HTTPS, proxies, and authentication
- Custom headers and arbitrary request data

Usage

Basic invocation:

    bat [flags] [METHOD] URL [ITEM [ITEM]]

Examples

Hello world:

    $ bat beego.me

Send JSON data:

    $ bat PUT example.org name=John email=john@example.org

Submit a form (example):

    $ bat -form=true POST example.org hello=World

Download a file:

    $ bat -download=true example.org/file

For help, run:

    bat --help


--- ignore ---

out/

--- help ---
bat is a Go implemented CLI cURL-like tool for humans.

Usage:

	bat [flags] [METHOD] URL [ITEM [ITEM]]

flags:
  -a, -auth=USER[:PASS]       Pass a username:password pair as the argument
  -b, -bench=false            Sends bench requests to URL
  -b.N=1000                   Number of requests to run
  -b.C=100                    Number of requests to run concurrently
  -body=""                    Send RAW data as body
  -f, -form=false             Submitting the data as a form
  -j, -json=true              Send the data in a JSON object
  -p, -pretty=true            Print Json Pretty Format
  -i, -insecure=false         Allow connections to SSL sites without certs
  -proxy=PROXY_URL            Proxy with host and port
  -print="A"                  String specifying what the output should contain, default will print all information
         "H" request headers
         "B" request body
         "h" response headers
         "b" response body
  -v, -version=true           Show Version Number

METHOD:
  bat defaults to either GET (if there is no request data) or POST (with request data).

URL:
  The only information needed to perform a request is a URL. The default scheme is http://,
  which can be omitted from the argument; example.org works just fine.

ITEM:
  Can be any of:
    Query string   key=value
    Header         key:value
    Post data      key=value
    File upload    key@/path/file

Example:

	bat beego.me

more help information please refer to https://github.com/astaxie/bat

</output>

package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/tls"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

type requestPlan struct {
	request       *http.Request
	body          []byte
	files         map[string]string
	fields        map[string]string
	pendingUpload bool
}

func isMethod(s string) bool {
	switch strings.ToUpper(s) {
	case "GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", "OPTIONS", "HEAD":
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func normalizeURL(s string) string {
	if strings.HasPrefix(s, ":") {
		s = "localhost" + s
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(s, "http://") && !strings.HasPrefix(s, "https://") {
		s = "http://" + s
	}
	return s
}

func makePlan(o options, args []string) requestPlan {
	if len(args) == 0 {
		usage()
	}
	method := ""
	if isMethod(args[0]) {
		method = strings.ToUpper(args[0])
		args = args[1:]
		if len(args) == 0 {
			fatalAt("filter.go:35", "Miss the URL")
		}
	}
	if args[0] == "" {
		usage()
	}
	address := normalizeURL(args[0])
	if _, err := url.Parse(address); err != nil {
		fatalAt("bat.go:158", err.Error())
	}
	items := args[1:]
	if method == "" {
		method = "GET"
		for _, item := range items {
			if strings.Count(item, "=") == 1 || strings.Count(item, "@") == 1 {
				method = "POST"
				break
			}
		}
	}

	params := make(map[string]string)
	files := make(map[string]string)
	type headerItem struct{ key, value string }
	var headers []headerItem
	for _, item := range items {
		if k, v, found := strings.Cut(item, ":"); found {
			headers = append(headers, headerItem{k, v})
		} else if strings.Contains(item, "@") && !o.JSON {
			if !o.Form {
				fatalAt("http.go:52", "file upload only support in forms style: -f=true")
			}
			k, v, _ := strings.Cut(item, "@")
			files[k] = v
		} else if k, v, found := strings.Cut(item, "="); found {
			params[k] = v
		}
	}

	var data []byte
	contentType := ""
	pendingUpload := false
	jsonMode := o.JSON || (method != "GET" && !o.Form)
	formMethod := method == "POST" || method == "PUT" || method == "PATCH"
	if method == "GET" && len(params) > 0 {
		var encoded []string
		for key, value := range params {
			encoded = append(encoded, url.QueryEscape(key)+"="+url.QueryEscape(value))
		}
		text := strings.Join(encoded, "&")
		if strings.Contains(address, "?") {
			address += "&" + text
		} else {
			address += "?" + text
		}
	} else if method != "GET" && !o.Form && len(params) > 0 {
		var b bytes.Buffer
		_ = json.NewEncoder(&b).Encode(params)
		data = b.Bytes()
		contentType = "application/json"
	} else if o.Form && formMethod && o.Body == "" {
		if len(files) > 0 {
			pendingUpload = true
		} else if len(params) > 0 {
			var encoded []string
			for key, value := range params {
				encoded = append(encoded, url.QueryEscape(key)+"="+url.QueryEscape(value))
			}
			data = []byte(strings.Join(encoded, "&"))
			contentType = "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
		}
	}
	if o.Body != "" {
		data = []byte(o.Body)
	}
	r, err := http.NewRequest(method, address, nil)
	if err != nil {
		fatalAt("bat.go:158", err.Error())
	}
	if len(data) != 0 {
		r.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(data))
		r.ContentLength = int64(len(data))
	}
	// Request bodies cannot be rewound for a 307/308 redirect.
	r.GetBody = nil
	if jsonMode {
		r.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
	} else {
		r.Header.Set("Accept", "*/*")
	}
	r.Header.Set("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate")
	for _, h := range headers {
		if h.key == "Host" {
			r.Host = h.value
		} else {
			r.Header.Set(h.key, h.value)
		}
	}
	if r.Header.Get("User-Agent") == "" {
		r.Header.Set("User-Agent", "bat/"+version)
	}
	if contentType != "" {
		r.Header.Set("Content-Type", contentType)
	}
	if o.Auth != "" {
		pair := strings.Split(o.Auth, ":")
		if len(pair) == 2 {
			r.SetBasicAuth(pair[0], pair[1])
		} else {
			r.SetBasicAuth(o.Auth, "")
		}
	}
	return requestPlan{request: r, body: data, files: files, fields: params, pendingUpload: pendingUpload}
}

func makeClient(o options) (*http.Client, *http.Transport) {
	t := &http.Transport{
		DialContext:     (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}).DialContext,
		TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: o.Insecure},
		Proxy:           http.ProxyFromEnvironment,
	}
	if o.Proxy != "" {
		u, err := url.Parse(o.Proxy)
		if err != nil {
			fatalAt("bat.go:182", "Proxy Url parse err"+err.Error())
		}
		// Only the socks5 spelling selects SOCKS; other unfamiliar schemes
		// retain the HTTP proxy behavior.
		if u.Scheme == "socks5h" {
			u.Scheme = "http"
		}
		t.Proxy = http.ProxyURL(u)
	}
	return &http.Client{Transport: t}, t
}
